stimulus.text:
“Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof; or abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press; or the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.”

—First Amendment to the Constitution, proposed September 25, 1789, ratified December 15, 1791
stimulus.source_note: First Amendment to the Constitution, proposed September 25, 1789, ratified December 15, 1791. Public domain.

source: original; stimulus viewed before writing — First Amendment to the Constitution, proposed September 25, 1789, ratified December 15, 1791, public domain.

primary_sources: First Amendment to the Constitution (proposed September 25, 1789; ratified December 15, 1791)

stem: The passage protects “the right of the people peaceably to assemble.” Which of the following best shows that right in use?

options.text: A crowd blocking a road so no one can pass
options.misconception: Blocking a road is not peaceable assembly; the passage protects peaceable gathering.

options.text: Citizens gathering in a town square to sign a petition
A newspaper printing an editorial against the president
options.misconception: A newspaper editorial shows freedom of the press, not assembly.

options.text: A church holding a service on a Sunday morning
options.misconception: A church service shows free exercise of religion, not assembly.

rationales.B: Gathering in a square to sign a petition is people assembling peaceably, and petitioning is the next freedom the passage names.
rationales.A: Blocking a road is not peaceable, so it falls outside the right the passage protects.
rationales.C: An editorial shows freedom of the press, a different freedom in the same passage.
rationales.D: A church service shows free exercise of religion, a different freedom in the same passage.
rationales.general:
1. The passage protects the right of the people to assemble peaceably.
2. Citizens gathering in a square to sign a petition are doing just that.
3. A blocked road is not peaceable, and an editorial and a church service show other freedoms.
4. So the gathering in the square is the one that shows assembly in use.
Remember: each freedom in the First Amendment has its own shape; match the act to the freedom.
